title: Keyword search vs. semantic search
intro: The same query, run twice against the same catalogue. On the left, the keyword engine matches words. On the right, semantic search matches meaning — it compares the embedding of your query with the embedding of every product, so it can answer a request whose words appear nowhere in the catalogue.
placeholder: Describe what you are looking for…
languageNote: ⚠️ This catalogue is not in English. The deployed embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) only understands English, and the product names are English in every catalogue — so a query in another language will rank confidently but meaninglessly. Switch to an English catalogue to see the comparison work.

keyword.title: Keyword search
keyword.subtitle: What this storefront ships today — BM25 over the indexed text fields.
keyword.emptyBody: Not one product contains these words. There is no spelling mistake to correct and no synonym configured, so the keyword engine has nothing to match on — the shopper hits a dead end.

vector.title: Semantic search
vector.subtitle: Vector similarity over the product embeddings, computed by OpenSearch kNN. It ranks the whole catalogue — it never filters, and never comes back empty.
vector.unavailableBody: The vector query returned nothing. Check that the premium GallyVectorSearchBundle is installed, that a model is deployed (make sf c=gally:vector-search:upload-model) and that the products carry embeddings.

footnote: Note the asymmetry: vector search ranks rather than filters. It returns the whole catalogue ordered by similarity and never reports “no results” — which is its strength on a query like these, and why a production setup usually applies a minimum score, or runs it only as a fallback when keyword search finds nothing.
